taxonomic_note: POWO accepts Achillea millefolium L. Historical North American A. occidentalis and A. millefolium var. occidentalis usages are concept-dependent; do not create synonym-based duplicate cards. FNA's broad A. millefolium complex and POWO's Texas introduced designation conflict for nativity interpretation.
look_here_first: Look at a fully developed stem leaf first: narrow outline but very finely divided into many tiny fernlike segments (usually 1–2-pinnately dissected). Then inspect the flat-topped cluster of numerous tiny composite heads. Check a single head from the side for several rows of overlapping phyllaries; do not infer native status or identity from white/pink color.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Calvin-approved Master Plant Pool row 14 (My iNaturalist Flora, Hays Local, Personal List); existing taxonomy review 2026-10-09
project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO explicitly treats Texas as introduced; FNA includes Texas within its broad A. millefolium treatment. Occurrence is not proof of native provenance. Do not count as target-zone native pending concept/provenance resolution.

morphology_keys.habit: Aromatic rhizomatous perennial herb; erect flowering stems, usually forming patches.
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate, deeply finely dissected, usually 1–2-pinnate, fernlike foliage; examine segments at magnification.
morphology_keys.heads: Many small capitula crowded in a relatively flat-topped corymb; usually 5–8 small ray florets around disk florets; involucral phyllaries commonly about 20–30 in several series.
morphology_keys.fruits: Small compressed cypselae roughly 1–2 mm, margins may be winged; inspect mature material rather than inferring from flowering heads.
best_field_traits: numerous small heads forming a flat-topped cluster
individual head with short rays and layered phyllaries

comparisons.key_distinctions: Anthemis cotula has larger solitary daisy-like heads with a more conspicuous ray circle, not many tiny heads packed in a flat-topped corymb. Tanacetum parthenium has broader lobed leaves and larger individual daisy heads. Artemisia ludoviciana has simple to shallowly lobed leaves and inconspicuous rayless heads. Check leaf architecture and individual head anatomy, not just white flower clusters.

diagnostic_image_plan.target: show successive orders of fine leaf dissection and attachment
count small rays and show several rows of phyllaries
show flat-topped compound cluster and alternate leaves
show size, shape and margins with scale
